get.description: Returns all of the caller's default agents, ordered by source. Not paginated: a user names one source per client it runs and the app wants the whole set at once.
Returns the caller's default agent for one source. A source that holds no default is reported as 404.

put.description: Upserts the caller's default agent for one source: the agent of an existing source is overwritten, a source that does not exist is created. The agent has to be one the caller may use: its own, or one another user shares.

delete.description: Hard delete of the caller's default agent for one source. A source that has no default is reported as 404.

get.description: Returns the caller's own agents plus every agent another user shares, ordered by name. A shared agent carries `is_public` true and `owned` false, and cannot be changed by anyone but its owner. Not paginated: a user has few of them.

post.description: The agent belongs to the caller. `is_public` shares it with every other user and is reserved to superusers. Answers 201 with a Location header pointing at the new agent.

get.description: Returns the id and name of the caller's own agents plus the ones other users share, ordered by name then id. The rest of each agent is left out. Not paginated: a user has few of them.
Returns an agent the caller may use: one it owns, or one another user shares. An agent the caller may not use is reported as 404.

put.description: Every field is optional and a field that is absent is left untouched. `is_public` shares the agent with every other user and is reserved to superusers. Another user's agent is reported as 404, so only the owner changes a shared one.

delete.description: Hard delete of one of the caller's agents. Another user's agent is reported as 404.

get.description: Returns the caller's keys, newest first. The keys themselves are not part of the response: only the prefix each was created with.

post.description: The key belongs to the caller. The response is the only place the key itself is ever returned; only its hash is stored, so a lost key cannot be recovered, only replaced.

delete.description: Soft delete: the key stops authenticating at once, is left out of the listing, and the row stays behind for audit with the time and the reason. Another user's key is reported as 404, and deleting a deleted key is a no-op.

patch.description: A field that is absent keeps its stored value. Setting expires_at is also how a lapsed key is renewed: the key is then active and usable again, and null makes it never expire. Switching a lapsed key on without moving its expiry is refused. A key that was deleted is hidden and cannot be updated. Another user's key is reported as 404.

post.description: Answers 204 whether or not the email exists, so the endpoint cannot be used to enumerate accounts. A reset link is generated for an existing active account only.
Accepts a username or an email as login. A wrong password, an unknown account and a deactivated account all answer 401 with the same body.
Consumes the refresh token and returns a new pair. The old token cannot be used again.
Creates an ordinary user and returns it. No token is issued; the caller logs in afterwards.
Consumes the reset token and stores the new password. An unknown, expired or already used token answers 400 with the same body. No refresh token is revoked.

get.description: Requires a bearer token. Returns groups only, never their members.

post.description: Superuser only. Answers 201 with a Location header pointing at the new group.

get.description: Requires a bearer token.

delete.description: Superuser only. Hard delete: the group and its memberships are removed.

get.description: Superuser only: the response carries user DTOs, so a plain token must not reach it.
get.summary: List the members of a group

put.description: Superuser only. Idempotent: adding an existing member answers 204 as well.

delete.description: Superuser only. Removing a membership that does not exist answers 204 as well.

get.description: Returns pong. Does not touch PostgreSQL or Redis.

Returns the caller's own providers plus every provider another user shares, ordered by the priority that applies to the caller: its own `priority_override` on a shared provider when one is set, the provider's own `priority` when the caller owns it, and `-99` on a shared provider the caller never ordered. A shared provider carries `is_public` true and `owned` false, and only its owner changes its fields. Not paginated: a user has few of them.

post.description: The provider belongs to the caller. `is_public` shares it with every other user and is reserved to superusers. Answers 201 with a Location header pointing at the new provider.

get.description: Returns name and model_name for the caller's own providers plus the ones other users share, in the same order as GET /api/providers. The remaining provider fields, credentials included, are left out. Not paginated: a user has few of them.

Returns a provider the caller may use: one it owns, or one another user shares. api_key is included, since the client needs it to reach the model. A provider the caller may not use is reported as 404.

put.description: A field that is absent keeps its stored value; sending null clears a nullable field. `is_public` shares the provider with every other user and is reserved to superusers. Another user's provider is reported as 404, so only the owner changes a shared one.

delete.description: Hard delete of one of the caller's providers. Another user's provider is reported as 404.

put.description: Sets the priority the caller uses to order a provider another user shared. The provider's own fields, credentials included, stay with its owner; only the caller's ordering changes, and every other user is left alone. A provider the caller owns is reported as 400 (its priority is its own field), a provider the caller may not use as 404.

get.description: Returns all of the caller's sessions, most recently updated first, without their messages. Not paginated: the app syncs its whole session set in one go. A source query keeps only sessions uploaded from that application; without one every source is returned.

parameters.description: Keep only sessions uploaded from this application
parameters.name: source

post.description: The session belongs to the caller. A uuid the caller brings is kept; one it does not is minted here. Answers 201 with a Location header pointing at the new session.

get.description: Returns one of the caller's sessions without its messages. Another user's session is reported as 404.

put.description: Every field is optional and a field that is absent is left untouched. A history replaces the session's messages wholesale. Another user's session is reported as 404.

delete.description: Hard delete of one of the caller's sessions, its messages included. Another user's session is reported as 404.

get.description: Returns all messages of one of the caller's sessions in the order they were sent. Not paginated: the app loads a session's whole history, which is also what its own file storage holds. Another user's session is reported as 404.
Returns the generated Swagger 2.0 document describing this API. Served without caching, so a viewer always sees the current API.

options.description: Answers the CORS preflight for the specification endpoints. Any origin may read the document, and GET is the only method offered.

get.description: Returns the generated Swagger 2.0 document describing this API. Served without caching, so a viewer always sees the current API.
Returns all of the caller's config entries, ordered by key. Not paginated: the app treats them as one local config file and syncs the whole set at once.

put.description: Upserts one config entry of the caller: the value of an existing key is overwritten, a key that does not exist is created.

delete.description: Hard delete of one of the caller's config entries.

get.description: Superuser only. Filters by is_active and searches username, email and display name with q.

parameters.description: Keep only active or only inactive users
parameters.name: is_active

parameters.description: Search term for username, email or display name
parameters.name: q

post.description: Superuser only. Answers 201 with a Location header pointing at the new user.

get.description: Returns the account behind the access token.

patch.description: Changes username, email and display name. Sending is_superuser is rejected with 403 rather than ignored.

put.description: Requires the current password. No refresh token is revoked, so other devices stay logged in.

get.description: Superuser only.

delete.description: Superuser only. Soft delete: the row stays and is_active becomes false. Use PATCH to restore. A caller cannot deactivate itself, and the last active superuser cannot be deactivated.

patch.description: Superuser only. Every field is optional; this is the only path that changes is_superuser. Is_active false deactivates the account and true restores it.

put.description: Superuser only. The current password is not required and no refresh token is revoked.

get.description: Returns the version of the running binary. It is injected at build time from the release tag, so a development build reports "dev". Does not touch PostgreSQL or Redis.

key.description:
Key is the plaintext key. Only the create response carries it: that is
the single moment the key exists outside its owner's hands.

priority_override.description:
PriorityOverride is the caller's own priority for a shared provider, or
null when the caller never ordered it. It is always null on a provider the
caller owns: that priority is edited through the provider.
